description: P-51D Mustang 1/4 scale, 120 cc class (plans/short-kit class: Chad Veich 1/4 plans, Jerry Bates 1/4, FokkeRC 1/4 short kit): 2.820 m span giant-scale P-51D Mustang, 120 cc gasoline. EXPERIMENTAL first physics estimate (P51-05), generated by research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py from full-size dimensions scaled to the kit; not flight-identified. Flaps and retracts are not simulated (gear DOWN drag). Visual geometry lives in assets/aircraft/p51d-mustang-120/geometry.json.

frames.body: simulation body axes FRD about the CG: x forward = -x_aft, y right, z down = -z_up

crash_hull.source: Points that hit the ground first (le frame) from assets/aircraft/p51d-mustang-120/geometry.json (P51-01: full-size P-51D dimensions scaled to the kit span): wing tip LE/TE (with dihedral), spinner tip, propeller disc bottom and lower quarters (a prop strike), rudder bottom TE, stab tips, fin top, canopy top, scoop bottom. The wheels are landing-gear contacts (P51-12)

mass_range.source: kit flying mass range 18.0-24.0 kg (source.json; CARF 2.54 m: 15-17 kg dry), widened for fuel and the virtual balancing mass of the reference build

aileron.source: asin(kit mm / local chord): Hangar 9 HAN4770 high rates (aileron 22 mm up, elevator 25 mm, rudder 55 mm) scaled by span 2.82/2.26 = 1.25; CARF (2.54 m) high rate: aileron 12.7 mm, elevator 19 mm up, rudder 51 mm

elevator.source: asin(kit mm / local chord): Hangar 9 HAN4770 high rates (aileron 22 mm up, elevator 25 mm, rudder 55 mm) scaled by span 2.82/2.26 = 1.25; CARF (2.54 m) high rate: aileron 12.7 mm, elevator 19 mm up, rudder 51 mm

rudder.source: asin(kit mm / local chord): Hangar 9 HAN4770 high rates (aileron 22 mm up, elevator 25 mm, rudder 55 mm) scaled by span 2.82/2.26 = 1.25; CARF (2.54 m) high rate: aileron 12.7 mm, elevator 19 mm up, rudder 51 mm

aero.source: Derived from the scaled geometry by research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py (Helmbold/DATCOM, tail volume, strip theory, drag build-up); report research/p51/p51-05/derivation.md. Not flight-identified: EXPERIMENTAL.

CL_max.source: 15 % laminar section clmax ~1.3 at Re 7e5 x 0.9 for the wing, flaps up; no polar identified

CL_min.source: cambered section: inverted stall earlier than upright

stall_blend_width.source: NACA TN 1945: at Re 0.7-1e6 the 15 % 6-series stall is rounded (cl flat over ~4 deg, mild drop); which part of the span stalls first comes from the strip offsets (aero.surfaces.wing_station_incidence)

sideslip_blend.source: Sideslip range where the linear beta terms (CYb, Clb, Cnb) give way to their sin(beta) form, finite and restoring up to knife edge

conventions.rates: p_hat = p·b/(2V), q_hat = q·c/(2V), r_hat = r·b/(2V)
conventions.elevator: per radian, positive = trailing edge DOWN (dCm/dElev < 0)
conventions.aileron: per radian per surface, positive = trailing edge DOWN; right and left listed separately
conventions.rudder: per radian, positive = trailing edge LEFT (dCn/dRud < 0)
conventions.axes: lift, drag, side force in wind axes; roll, pitch, yaw moments in body axes about the aero reference point

CL0.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: cambered wing at +1 deg incidence + tail at zero body alpha

CLa.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: Helmbold wing x cos2(dihedral) + downwashed tail

CLadot.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 2 eta CLa_h Sh/S l_h/c deps/dalpha

CLq.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail volume + DATCOM wing term

CLde.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail slope x elevator effectiveness

CLda_each.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: strip theory over the aileron span

CD0.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: component drag build-up at 25 m/s with the gear DOWN (retracts not simulated), see derivation.md

CL_minD.source: cambered laminar section: minimum drag near half the zero-alpha wing lift

CDda_each.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e (via the Stik data file); second-order control drag

CDdr.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e (via the Stik data file); second-order control drag

CDde.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e (via the Stik data file); second-order control drag

Clb.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 5 deg dihedral (strip theory) + wing at CL_ref + low-wing interference + fin

Clp.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: strip theory with taper + stab + fin

Cldr.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: rudder side force x fin height above the ARP

Cm0.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: wing Cm_ac (parabolic camber) + tail at zero body alpha, about the ARP

Cma.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail about the wing-body ac; the CG transfer gives the static margin

Cmq.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail damping about the CG (undownwashed tail slope) x1.1 for wing/fuselage

Cmde.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: elevator lift x tail arm from the ARP

Cmda_each.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: aileron lift increment at its thin-airfoil centre, arm from the ARP

Cnb.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: fin only (v1 contract: equals the vertical surface)

Cnr.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: fin + wing profile drag + fuselage (-0.02 estimated)

Cnda_right.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: adverse yaw 2 K CL_ref Clda, K 0.15 (Nelson, AR 5.8, taper 0.48)

Cndr.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: rudder side force x fin arm from the ARP (must equal the vertical surface)

wing_aileron_effectiveness.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: |Clda_right| 2n b / (CLa sum(y)) over the loader's equal-area tapered strips

wing_station_incidence.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: per-strip angle offsets root -> tip, zero mean: linear washout + Schrenk loading + Re-dependent section clmax (NACA TN 1945); see derivation.md 'stall'

propulsion.description: 120 cc gasoline twin turning a 4-blade 26x12. Shaft balance (rpm from engine torque against propeller torque), blade-element tables calibrated on Mejzlik's 26x12 2- and 3-blade data, down and right thrust, propeller normal force and P-factor, tail slipstream with swirl (research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py, P51-06/P51-12).

engine.name: Desert Aircraft DA-120 (121 cc twin, 2.45 kg with ignition) or DLE-120

peak_power.source: DA-120 11.7 hp, desertaircraft.com/products/da-120 (2026-10-06): the maker's rating; the installed curve below is lower

peak_power_rpm.source: DA-120 top of the 1300-6900 rpm range (desertaircraft.com)

max_rpm_static.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: full-throttle shaft balance at rest (shaft model)

idle_rpm.source: static idle: DA-120 range starts at 1300 rpm (desertaircraft.com); set a little above for a large propeller

lag_time_constant.source: D5 lag model, unused while the shaft model is present (kept for the format)

power_curve.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: installed full-throttle brake power: generic two-stroke torque shape (estimated; no DA-120 dyno curve published) scaled to the measured anchor, a 28x10 at 6550 rpm static (Mejzlik 28x10 Cp 0.0238 -> 6901 W)

friction_torque.source: friction and pumping ~12 % of the brake torque at 6900 rpm (YASim 8 %; research synthesis 10-15 %)

idle_power.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: closed-throttle admitted power: holds 1400 rpm static

peak_indicated_power.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: brake + friction power at the curve's peak: the open throttle never limits

propeller.name: 4-blade 26x12 (scale look; heavy for a 120 cc: Biela rates its 26x12 4-blade for 150-160 cc, the DA-120 list gives 3-blade 26x12 / 27x12)
propeller.rotation: clockwise seen from behind (standard tractor): the reaction torque rolls the airplane left

ct_table.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: blade-element/momentum (research/p51/p51-06/bem.py), pitch x1.441 and chord x0.581 fitted to Mejzlik 26x12 2B/3B tables (rms 6.5 %); tabulated into the windmilling branch

cp_table.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: same calibrated blade-element model; Cp < 0 = windmilling

rotating_inertia.source: 4 x Mejzlik's mean per-blade inertia (26x12 2B/3B datasheets) + spinner shell + crank and flywheel 0.002

thrust_line_offset.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: propeller disc centre (thrust line) relative to the inventory CG; [x_aft, y_right, z_up]

thrust_angles.source: down 1.75 deg (Top Flite Giant P-51D manual), right 1 deg (Ziroli 98 in plans); no published full-size or 1/4-scale value

normal_force.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: McCormick blade-element normal force per rad of disc angle of attack (Selig, AIAA 2010-7938), x rho n2 D4; solidity 0.112

pfactor_moment.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: McCormick P-factor yawing moment per rad of disc angle of attack (Selig, AIAA 2010-7938), x rho n2 D5

hub.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: propeller disc centre on the thrust line (le frame)

wash_factor.source: velocity added at the tail per disc induced velocity w: 0.8 static, 1.8 at mass-flow ratio >= 0.75 (Selig, AIAA 2010-7938, Fig. 5; ideal 2)

swirl_factor.source: part of the propeller's angular momentum that reaches the tail (wing and fuselage straighten the rest): research synthesis 0.5-0.8; Selig: the swirl offsets ~40 % of the torque roll

vertical_drift.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 1 - d(eps)/d(alpha): the wake drifts with the downwashed flow

landing_gear.description: P51-12: taildragger, two main wheels and a steerable tail wheel (E1 spring-dampers, E2 tyre friction, E3 field surfaces). Retracts are not simulated: the gear stays down.

position.source: wheel bottom from geometry.json (axle station and height measured on the AN 01-60-3 three-view, track 142 in full size per NACA, wheel 6.75 in)

stiffness.source: E1 rule: heave ω·dt 0.09 at 240 Hz (Σk = 10031 N/m for 21.50 kg), split by the static load (12.2 % on the tail wheel) so all three wheels sag alike (21 mm); softer than a real oleo, which a 240 Hz explicit tick cannot resolve

damping.source: damping ratio 0.3 of the loader's m/3 share: sprung oleo legs and tyres, little hydraulic damping in RC retract struts

max_compression.source: breaking travel: a level touchdown at about 2.5 m/s sink reaches it (½mv² against the springs with the static sag); RC practice, not measured
